title: GitHub Repos
subtitle: Create, fork, and navigate repositories on GitHub
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: Git is a local tool. To collaborate with others, deploy code, or contribute to open-source projects, you need a shared hosting platform.
whyItExists.solution: GitHub hosts Git repositories with a web UI, issue tracking, CI/CD, code review, and collaboration tools. It's where most of the world's open-source code lives.
whyItExists.whenToUse: For every project you want to share, back up, or deploy. For any open-source contribution.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Private/proprietary work may use GitHub Private or a self-hosted alternative (GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea).

explainModes.beginner: GitHub is a website that stores your Git repos online. You push code up from your laptop and it appears on GitHub where others can see it, comment on it, and use it.
explainModes.simple: Create a repo on github.com/new. Add it as a remote: git remote add origin <url>. Push: git push -u origin main. Fork: copies someone else's repo to your account. Star: bookmarks a repo. Issues: track bugs and feature requests.
explainModes.standard: GitHub repos have: Code tab (files, branches, commits), Issues (bugs, features), Pull Requests (code review), Actions (CI/CD), Settings (branch protection, webhooks). Forking creates a copy of a repo under your account — you have full write access. After forking, clone your fork, make changes, then open a PR to the original repo.
explainModes.technical: GitHub's fork is a server-side clone — it shares the git objects with the upstream but has its own refs/heads. Syncing a fork: git remote add upstream <original-url>, git fetch upstream, git merge upstream/main. GitHub API (api.github.com) allows programmatic access to all repo operations. GitHub CLI (gh) brings GitHub's PR/issue workflow to the terminal.
explainModes.deepDive: GitHub's REST and GraphQL APIs power integrations, bots, and automation. Personal Access Tokens (PATs) or GitHub Apps authenticate API access. GitHub's Dependabot automatically opens PRs for dependency updates. Repository topics and keywords improve discoverability. GitHub Codespaces spins up a VS Code environment in the browser backed by the repo. GitHub Discussions is a forum-style alternative to Issues for community Q&A.

content.code:
# Via GitHub CLI (recommended)
gh repo create my-project --public
gh repo create my-project --private

# Then push an existing local repo:
git remote add origin https://github.com/yourname/my-project.git
git push -u origin main

# Or clone right after creating:
gh repo create my-project --public --clone
cd my-project

content.text: Forking copies a repo to your GitHub account so you can make changes. You then open a Pull Request to propose your changes to the original repo.

content.code:
# 1. Fork on GitHub (click the Fork button)

# 2. Clone YOUR fork (not the original)
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/repo.git
cd repo

# 3. Add the original as 'upstream' remote
git remote add upstream https://github.com/ORIGINAL-OWNER/repo.git
git remote -v
# origin   https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/repo.git (your fork)
# upstream https://github.com/ORIGINAL-OWNER/repo.git (original)

# 4. Create a branch, make changes, push to YOUR fork
git switch -c fix/typo-in-readme
# ... make changes ...
git push origin fix/typo-in-readme

# 5. Open PR on GitHub from your fork to the original

# 6. Keep your fork in sync with upstream
git fetch upstream
git switch main
git merge upstream/main
git push

questions.question: What is a GitHub fork?
options: A local copy of a repo
A server-side copy of a repo under your GitHub account
questions.explanation: A fork is a server-side copy of a repo on GitHub. It lives under your account, you have full write access, and you can open Pull Requests from your fork to the original (upstream) repo.

faq.q: What is the difference between a fork and a clone?
faq.a: A fork happens on GitHub's servers — it creates a copy under your account. A clone happens on your machine — it downloads a repo locally. When contributing to open-source, you typically fork first, then clone your fork.

faq.q: How do I install the GitHub CLI?
faq.a: macOS: brew install gh. Windows: winget install --id GitHub.cli. Ubuntu: sudo apt install gh. After installing, run gh auth login to authenticate with your GitHub account.

examples: All major open-source projects (React, Vue, Linux) accept contributions via fork + PR
GitHub Stars act as bookmarks — 1k+ stars signals a widely-used and trusted project
